In just days, our system went from 2 agents (voice, PPT) to 4 (voice, PPT, web search, browser-use) — five roles counting the human, collaborating asynchronously yet real-time. New agents register and join with ease, and latency stays low. The human speaks and listens to the voice agent, which is voice-connected to every other agent and knows when to speak up on its own.
It all runs on a consumer-grade laptop, under 16GB of VRAM: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B for recognition, lightweight IndexTTS-2.5 for synthesis, no fine-tuning — just the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash API. In a room that is anything but quiet, the latest version filters out most of the noise.
Today's AI, I believe, is about two things: understanding and interaction. Understanding pursues the upper bound of intelligence; interaction should center on humans. Its value: first, once models understand, interaction decides how efficiently humans understand what they produce — in essence, education. Second, in the coming era of embodied intelligence, voice remains the most natural modality between humans and robots, just as it is between people.
The demo: in minutes, with voice alone, I controlled all three agents — even a drive can become productive conversation.
